reviewerLens: Independent refutation of browser UX/accessibility findings

verdicts.claim: Core timer actions lose keyboard focus when their initiating button changes action.
verdicts.refutationAttempt: Checked whether the focus key matches an equivalent rendered control or whether a dialog fallback moves focus. Commit/start/pause/resume all replace their triggering action button; no matching target and no dialog fallback exist.
verdicts.evidence: Activated each of commit, start, pause, and resume with keyboard Enter in Chromium. document.activeElement.tagName was BODY after each transition.
verdicts.scope: Keyboard continuity and visible focus; action itself still completes and saves.

verdicts.claim: The undo control remains clickable above an open modal and can replace the modal workflow.
verdicts.refutationAttempt: Checked aria-modal, focus trapping, inherited inert state, CSS pointer events, stacking, and actual elementFromPoint hit testing. aria-modal and the keyboard trap do not disable mouse/touch interaction, while the toast button explicitly restores pointer events.
verdicts.evidence: After rating then opening options at 390x844, undo is outside the dialog, has no inert ancestor, toast z-index is 6 versus backdrop 5, and elementFromPoint selects undo. A normal Playwright click on undo removes the modal and returns the session to review.
verdicts.scope: Background-action isolation and dialog overlay; no duplicate rating or data corruption observed.

verdicts.claim: Reloading a history page renders the timer while the URL still says #history.
verdicts.refutationAttempt: Checked whether popstate runs on initial page load or whether initialization restores history.state. Startup recognizes only #calendar, and does not restore the stored history date. popstate contains separate routing but does not repair initial load.
verdicts.evidence: Navigated through calendar into a saved session history, confirmed .history-page, then reloaded. URL stayed index.html#history; .history-page count became zero and .timer-page count became one.
verdicts.scope: Route and selection persistence; session history remains saved.

verdicts.claim: Importing JSON null displays an internal JavaScript TypeError instead of a useful invalid-backup message.
verdicts.refutationAttempt: Checked error handling and whether null causes an uncaught error, broken state, or restore mutation. The TypeError is caught and displayed by toast; no restore confirmation opens and existing data is unchanged.
verdicts.evidence: Uploaded a file whose complete contents are null. The toast reads Cannot read properties of null (reading 'kind'). Restore confirmation count remains zero.
verdicts.scope: Error-message quality only; any claim of app crash or data loss is refuted.
